sentence_stem: Having been informed of the delay,
correct_completion: the passengers waited patiently in the lounge.
full_sentence: Having been informed of the delay, the passengers waited patiently in the lounge.
acceptable_variants: the passengers settled down to wait in the lounge.
the passengers decided to stay in the lounge until the train arrived.

options.text: the train had already left the station.
options.why_wrong: This states a fact about the train, but the perfect passive participle requires a reaction by the subject, so the main clause must describe what the passengers did.

options.text: the passengers waited patiently in the lounge.
the announcement was made in the morning.
options.why_wrong: The stem already expresses the passive idea of being informed, so repeating the announcement in the main clause does not complete the logical link.

options.text: the passengers had to be informed again.
options.why_wrong: This repeats the passive idea from the stem and makes the sequence of events illogical.

grammar_focus: Perfect passive participle clauses expressing a completed event before the main clause
explanation: The perfect passive participle 'having been informed' shows that the event in the first clause is completed before the action in the main clause. The main clause must describe a logical reaction of the subject to that event. Learners whose first language expresses this sequence with a separate time-ordered sentence may find the compressed participle form less natural at first, so comparing the two structures helps.
translation: Po poinformowaniu o opóźnieniu pasażerowie cierpliwie czekali w poczekalni.
